newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CROWN SHAKEN BY INTEREST RATE JITTERS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CROWN SHAKEN BY INTEREST RATE JITTERS.

text.p: The Czech crown slumped on Thursday against its mark/dollar peg amid nervousness that the Czech National Bank (CNB) was preparing to cut interest rates.

The crown, which is fixed daily against a mark/dollar basket, was trading down at 29.730 to the dollar and 17.309 to the mark in mid-afternoon trading from 29.45 to the dollar and 17.16 to the mark late on Wednesday.
The drop knocked more than a full percentage point off the crown's value against the central bank's mark/dollar basket.

Dealers said they did not expect, though they could not rule out the possibility, that the CNB would cut rates at its weekly board meeting later on Thursday but many said it was more likely that the central bank would move next week.
"I think the market is nervous and the nervousness could still be there till next week when the government will announce some economic measures," said Tomas Becvar of Komercni Banka.
The government is due to announce a package of measures to reinvigorate growth next Wednesday when many anlaysts expect the CNB to move as well.

The economy has run into serious problems in recent months with the latest batch of bad news coming on Wednesday morning when official figures showed industrial production falling 5.8 percent year-on-year in February.

Senior government officials have been vocal in blaming the central bank's highly restrictive monetary policy for the economic slowdown and many foreign exchange dealers are now convinced that the CNB will cut rates soon.
"I think the market is more or less positioned for a drop in interest rates," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

In an effort to rein in the money supply and bring inflation down, the Czech central bank last summer raised the discount rate by one percentage point to 10.5 percent and minimum reserve requirements were increased to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent.

The moves have been successful with M2 money growth slowing to 7.8 percent in December from over 20 percent before monetary policy was tightened, and inflation dropping to 6.8 percent in February from around 10 percent a year ago.

The sense that a rate cut might be on the cards was heightened when the Czech news agency CTK quoted Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik on Thursday as saying that the central bank and the government agreed to coordinate their economic policies in a late night meeting.
Korous said he expected the CNB to cut rates by around 50 basis points at first, perhaps followed by further moves later in the year.
